analysis:
This PR moves the release toolchain pin from SDK 27.0 / Swift 6.4 to SDK 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2. It also adds a two-mode selector. I examined the following changes. (1) scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh, head lines 1-163. It now enumerates installed Xcode*.app bundles, newest first, and exports DEVELOPER_DIR through GITHUB_ENV when it picks a different Xcode than the image's. It parses the Swift version by regex and normalizes the SDK version. It links the swift wrapper from the script's own directory instead of $GITHUB_WORKSPACE. The candidate paths come from the runner image's /Applications, or from DARKBLOOM_XCODE_APPLICATIONS and DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT, which are CI-controlled variables. I found no attacker-controlled input path, so there is no GITHUB_ENV injection concern from the evidence shown. (2) scripts/provider_release_resume/identity.py line 82. The recorded build_sdk_version is now '27.2'. (3) The docs/operations/provider-release.md and mise.toml version bumps are documentation and pin changes only. scripts/test-provider-release-toolchain.py is metadata only, with no content supplied.

Open integration question: the script's default mode is 'qualification', which still accepts SDK 27.0 and Swift 6.4.x. The 'release' mode (SDK 27.2 and Swift 6.4.2 only) applies only if the release, qualification, and signing workflows export DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN=release. Those workflow files are not in this batch, so I cannot confirm that signed production builds cannot silently fall back to the looser mode (T-034, T-054 build-identity integrity). Also, identity.py hardcodes 27.2 for resumed runs. A retained unsigned artifact built under SDK 27.0 would be mislabeled or rejected downstream. That is an availability or consistency matter rather than a confirmed security regression. The next pass should check the .github/workflows/release-*.yml env wiring and the resume or verify scripts that compare build_sdk_version with the recorded SDK. The threat model's attestation and qualification entries (A-017, T-054) do not need changes because the build-identity registration flow is unchanged.
